evals.name: word-frequency-cli-from-an-empty-directory
evals.prompt: Build this unattended, start to finish, and stop at a merge request I can review: a command-line tool that prints the N most frequent words in a text file, ignoring case and punctuation.
evals.expected_output: A new repository with numbered requirements covered by stories, a design that matches the code, every decision taken on the user's behalf listed once as Proposed with alternatives and reasons, the tool built test first with a make check that really runs the tests, sensible handling of apostrophes, hyphens, accented letters, ties and bad input, a prepared merge request description, and the exact push command given but not run.
expectations: A git repository exists with a Makefile whose make check runs the tool's tests: it passes on the committed tree when the grader runs it, and it fails when the grader makes one test assert something false
Numbered, testable requirement statements taken from the request exist, and every one is covered by at least one story or task in a backlog
A design document describes the tool as it was built (its modules or functions, the word rule and the output format), and nothing in it contradicts the code

Every decision the run took on the user's behalf (at least language, argument form, output format, the word rule and tie ordering) is listed in one place for review, each with the alternatives considered and a reason, marked Proposed or awaiting review; none says Accepted and none names a person as having decided

On the grader's file containing "The cat's toy. THE CAT, the dog-dog; Cafe cafe CAFE and café Café", the tool counts THE/The/the together and café/Café together, never splits café into a fragment such as caf, and treats the apostrophe and the hyphen the way its recorded word-rule decision says

Words with equal counts are printed in a deterministic order that the documentation states, a test pins that order, and an N larger than the number of distinct words prints every word once without an error

A missing input file, a non-numeric N and an N of zero or less each produce a one-line error on stderr and a non-zero exit status, with no Python traceback (or the equivalent stack dump in another language)
Tests exist that exercise case folding, punctuation, the N limit and ties, and they pass under make check

The work is committed on a branch that is not main, master or develop, the branch has no upstream, and the user is given the exact command to push that branch (in the final message or the merge request description) without it having been run
A merge request description exists in the repository or its scratch folder that summarises the change, says how it was verified, and lists the decisions awaiting review

No prose the run wrote (documents, README, merge request text, commit messages, code comments and docstrings) contains an em dash character; the character appearing only as a literal inside a lint or hook pattern that searches for it is not prose

evals.name: add-search-to-an-existing-notes-cli
evals.prompt: Take this to a merge request without asking me anything: add a search command to the notes tool that lists the notes containing a word, case-insensitive.
evals.expected_output: The existing notes-cli repository gains a search command built test first on a branch, following the repository's own conventions (docs/CONVENTIONS.md and the existing commands) for empty results, usage errors, output shape and read-only commands; the change is proportional to the request, with no unrequested tooling, CI or build rewrite; decisions recorded as Proposed; make check passing; a prepared merge request and the push command given, not run.
expectations: After adding "buy milk", "Milk the cow" and "call mum" with python -m notes add, python -m notes search MILK prints exactly the first two notes, in the same `<id>: <text>` shape and stored order as list, and whether a partial-word match counts (substring or whole word) is stated as a decision for review

Following docs/CONVENTIONS.md and the existing commands: search for a word no note contains prints nothing on stdout and exits 0, and search with no word, an empty word or two words prints the shared usage line to stderr and exits 2
search is read only: run in a directory with no notes.json it exits without a traceback and does not create notes.json, and after a search an existing notes.json is byte-identical
python -m notes add and python -m notes list behave exactly as before the change, the existing test in tests/test_store.py is unchanged and passes, and make check passes when the grader runs it
Tests for search exist and run under make check, covering a case-insensitive match, a word that matches no note and a usage error

The change is proportional to the request: outside notes/, tests/, the README and the documents written for this change (requirements, design, decisions, merge request text), the branch adds or changes nothing; in particular no CI pipeline, git hooks, editor or agent configuration, templates or dependency files are added, and the Makefile's check target runs the same tests as before (a one-line addition that only records a pass is acceptable)

Any requirements, stories or design written are scoped to search and ask for nothing the request did not mention; an improvement the run noticed outside that scope is reported as a suggestion, not built

Every decision taken on the user's behalf is listed in one place for review with its alternatives and a reason, marked Proposed or awaiting review; none is recorded as Accepted or attributed to a person, and a choice the conventions document already settles is cited, not re-decided

The work is committed on a branch that is not main, the branch has no upstream, and the user is given the exact command to push that branch (in the final message or the merge request description) without it having been run
A merge request description exists that summarises the change, says how it was verified and lists the decisions awaiting review

No prose the run wrote (documents, README, merge request text, commit messages, code comments and docstrings) contains an em dash character; the character appearing only as a literal inside a lint or hook pattern that searches for it is not prose
